We had always believed that when alien life touched down on Earth, it would look at least something like us. A head, two arms, two legs. That kind of thing. That's why we had such a difficult time accepting it. At first we thought perhaps we discovered a new species of earthworm. They were a lot larger than your normal variety, sure. But besides clustering in groups, there wasn't much different between their biology and the biology of anything else on the planet.

It wasn't until someone saw them literally falling from the sky that we knew what they were. They didn't come in large ships like sci-fi had taught us they would. They came in cocoons. From what we now know, the worms feast on the nitrogen rich soil of planets like earth for thousands of years until all the nutrients of the soil are completely gone. Then, they secrete a type of jelly that mixes with the dead soil and forms a shell almost as tough as steel around them, and a chemical reaction near their tails allow them to blast off into space. While its unknown how intelligent the worms are, they do seem to possess some mechanism to determine where hospitable planets will be. Then, they travel space for hundreds or maybe even thousands of years until they land and the whole process starts over again. As far as we can tell, the worms are effectively immortal when it comes to the aging process.

During the Great California Quake of 2048, we discovered that they are extremely sensitive to seismic disturbances. Within minutes of the quake hitting, hundreds of the worms came burrowing out of the ground. They even came through the asphalt of the roads. The enormous worms, nearly a foot in diameter and ten feet in length, were then killed by the residents.

So we began building the Hunters: large, semi-autonomous robots that were not only able to detect the trace radiation given off by the worms, but also able to simulate earthquakes up to a mile with its giant hydraulic arms. Usually, two to five marksmen traveled with one to pick off the worms that came to the surface.

Though we have exterminated a great majority of the worms, we have no idea how many are left or even how their breeding process works. We hope that we are able to kill them all before they kill our planet. Sure, we tried to communicate, but they seem to be mindless eating machines even though they possess the ability to travel through space. So for now, we will use the Hunters and continue our crusade against them.
